relevance.rationale: JOIN CONFIRMED from front matter (arXiv identifier and two-author list match the registered entry). Three citation sites: appendix-standard-model/sm-colour-stabilizer-action.md:11 (a \cite for 'the 1 + 3 colour decomposition of O = C + C^3') and docstring mentions at QOU/MathlibExt/OctonionComplexStructure.lean:9 and QOU/MathlibExt/OctonionColourActionBaseModule.lean:10. LOAD-BEARING AND ACCURATE — and in fact better sourced here than at the earlier companion: §2 (p.3) states directly that the subgroup preserving the splitting C + C^3 is SU(3), and that the automorphisms acting on C + C^3 give SU(3) x SU(3)/Z_3 with the first factor identified as the colour group. That stabilizer statement is precisely what QOU/MathlibExt/OctonionSU3Stabilizer.lean formalizes as su(3) = ker(ev_e) inside the derivation algebra, so the citation underwrites the exact construction the Lean carries. The Z_6-quotient programme named in the registered entry's note also matches the document's abstract. Stylistic note: two of the three sites name the key inside a prose docstring in backtick form rather than as a '-- Ref:' line, so a Lean-side grep for the standard Ref form finds nothing.

keyResults.statement: Within the derivation algebra of the octonions, the subgroup preserving the splitting C + C^3 is SU(3); the automorphisms acting on C + C^3 give SU(3) x SU(3)/Z_3 with the first factor the colour group.
keyResults.useForFolio: The literature statement matching QOU's octonion colour stabilizer su(3) = ker(ev_e) as a Lie subalgebra of the derivation algebra — the source the stabilizer construction is modelled on.

proposedActions.rationale: OctonionComplexStructure.lean:9 and OctonionColourActionBaseModule.lean:10 name the key only inside prose docstrings, so the standard '-- Ref: [key]' grep does not find them. Add the canonical Ref lines so both files register as citation sites in the bibliography audits.
